subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals - HealthTech
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@healthtech.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@healthtech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals - HealthTech

Hi Sofia / Alex,

Thanks again for the time today - really productive conversation. Below is a succinct recap of what we heard, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we're aligned going into the eval.

Summary / pain points:
- Lack of consistent model-level observability across routes: token-level latency, per-prompt cost, and error breakdowns are spread across internal logs and ad-hoc dashboards.
- Regression detection gaps: No automated golden-prompt regression alerts or versioned evals tied to rollouts.
- Tracing hooks: instrumenting upstream services to correlate request traces (user -> prompt -> model variant) is manual and inconsistent.
- Eval orchestration: need a repeatable eval harness (golden prompt sets, pass/fail thresholds) before can approve new model variants.

Current stack:
- Frontend -> Python backend services -> Kinesis -> ingestion to internal analytics / Grafana
- Using internal feature store and some ad-hoc eval scripts (Jupyter) for quality checks
- Security team (cc'd later) requires SOC2 evidence and ability to restrict telemetry to customer-managed VPCs

Success criteria (what HealthTech needs to be comfortable):
1) Dashboards showing per-route latency, per-token cost, and per-prompt quality metrics (p50/p95, error breakdown by model).
2) Tracing hooks that surface request IDs and map to model variant and cached KV keys.
3) Eval harness: golden prompt sets, automated regression alerts (email + Slack), and nightly runs with historical baselines.
4) Rollout guardrails: canary thresholds, automatic rollback on quality regressions, and manual approval gates for production changes.

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Pre-built observability dashboards (token-cost, latency heatmaps, per-prompt quality) and tracing integration guidance.
- Eval templates: golden prompt sets + evaluation runner + regression alerting rules.
- Rollout policies: canary/A-B + automatic fallback to safe model variants; integration with your CI/CD for approvals.
- Security/compliance artifacts package and optional Private deployment for sensitive workloads.

Requested deliverables from Redwood for eval phase:
- Obs & eval plan (attached: obs-eval-plan.xlsx) with dashboard mockups and instrumentation checklist.
- Redwood evals checklist PDF (attached) with steps required from HealthTech (sample prompts, data retention preferences, tracing hook snippet).
- Proposed timeline: initial infra instrumentation this week, end-to-end demo of dashboards + eval runner next Wed (07/08), 2-week eval run after instrumentation.

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- HealthTech: share 2-3 representative golden prompts and a non-sensitive sample dataset (Alex) - due Tue 07/07.
- Marissa / Redwood: provide instrumentation snippet and dashboard links + schedule demo (Marissa) - proposed Wed 07/08 10:00 AM PT.
- Security: HealthTech security to confirm required evidence types; Redwood to deliver SOC2 summary and data-flow diagram (cc Lauren and Marcus).

Attachments: obs-eval-plan.xlsx, redwood-evals-checklist.pdf, redwood-product-architecture.pdf

If I missed anything, please flag and I can update. Looking forward to the demo.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@healthtech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Observability & evals - HealthTech

Thanks Marissa - this captures the conversation well. A few clarifications: 
- The golden prompts will be a mix of PHI-free product flows and synthetic variants; Alex will share the exact set by EOD Tue.
- For rollouts, our product team needs canary thresholds on both latency (p95 increase <= 10%) and quality (F1 drop <= 3%).
- Security: we do need documentation that telemetry can be routed to our VPC-only endpoint for the eval. Can you confirm?

We're available for the demo Wed 07/08 at 10:00 AM PT. Please send a calendar invite.

Best,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Product, HealthTech
sofia.ramos@healthtech.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@healthtech.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@healthtech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Observability & evals - HealthTech

Thanks Sofia - great, appreciate the thresholds. Quick responses inline and next steps: 
- VPC-only telemetry: yes - we can route observability data to a customer-managed VPC endpoint for the eval. Marcus (cc) will share the minimal network requirements and a short checklist.
- Canary thresholds: we'll pre-configure canary policy with the latency and quality thresholds you listed and make them editable during rollout.

Calendar invite: sent for Wed 07/08 10:00 AM PT (includes a short pre-demo checklist).

Next immediate items: Alex to drop golden prompts + sample by Tue EOD. Marcus to send VPC/network checklist today. I'll upload the obs-eval-plan.xlsx and redwood-evals-checklist.pdf to the Drive link and share after this thread.

See you on Wed - looking forward to the demo.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: HealthTech eval - immediate action items

Lauren / Marcus - short internal summary and asks so we can move quickly: 
- Marcus: please send the VPC instrumentation checklist and minimal firewall rules + port list. Also include the tracing hook snippet we discussed for mapping request IDs to model variant.
- Marcus / Product: prepare a quick demo flow: token-cost dashboard, per-prompt quality table, and a regression-alert example that triggers on a golden prompt drop.
- Lauren: I'll need the SOC2 summary and product architecture PDF (redwood-product-architecture.pdf) to attach to the security thread.
- I'll coordinate calendar + share Drive links.

I'll loop back once Marcus posts the checklist; want to be ready to handoff to their infra on Monday.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: HealthTech eval - immediate action items

On it - attaching the minimal network checklist here (obs-eval-plan.xlsx covers most details). Key notes: 
- Telemetry endpoint: allow outbound HTTPS to the VPC ingress IP (TLS required).
- Ports: 443 outbound; ephemeral for agent heartbeats (no inbound required).
- Tracing hook: include X-Request-ID and Redwood-Model-Variant headers; sample snippet:
  curl -X POST https://ingest.redwood.com/v1/trace -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"request_id": "{{request_id}}", "model_variant": "{{variant}}", "latency_ms": {{latency}}}'

I'll prep the demo widgets and regression alert example for Wed.

Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Product, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
